subproblem.title: Re-graphing a small-slope C^1 graph over a nearby n-plane T0 (slope <= 1/7)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (c : Rn n) (d : Rn ℓ) (r ε ϑ : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 / 24 → 0 ≤ ϑ → ϑ ≤ 1 / 12 → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 v (closedBall 0 r) → v 0 = 0 → (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ‖fderivWithin ℝ v (closedBall 0 r) x‖ ≤ ε) → (∀ x : Rn n, infDist (q (graphPoint x 0)) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ ϑ * ‖x‖) → y = q₀ (graphPoint c d) → ∃ f : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball c (r / 2)) ∧ (∀ w ∈ ball c (r / 2), ‖fderiv ℝ f w‖ ≤ 1 / 7) ∧ (∀ w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), ∃ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, y + q (graphPoint x (v x)) = q₀ (graphPoint w (f w)) ∧ ‖graphPoint x (v x)‖ ≤ r) ∧ (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ∀ (w : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), y + q (graphPoint x (v x)) = q₀ (graphPoint w b) → w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2) → b = f w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: B_s(x) is the closed ball and B°_s(x) the open ball; T0 := rotatedPlane q0; E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd. Norms of linear maps are operator norms. The sibling arp_rotatedPlane_graphPoint_coords n l supplies:
- (i) graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b);
- (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2;
- (iii) infDist(q0(graphPoint a b), T0) = |b|.
0. Coordinates. For z in R^{n+l} put pi z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).1 in R^n and sigma z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).2 in R^l. Both are continuous linear maps.
By (i): z = q0(graphPoint (pi z) (sigma z)); pi(q0(graphPoint a b)) = a; sigma(q0(graphPoint a b)) = b.
By (ii) and since q0 is an isometry, |z|^2 = |pi z|^2 + |sigma z|^2, so |pi z| <= |z| and |sigma z| <= |z|.
By (iii), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z|. Also pi y = c.
By (i), graphPoint is linear in the pair: graphPoint a b = graphPoint a 0 + graphPoint 0 b, graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b'), and graphPoint 0 0 = 0.
By (ii), |graphPoint a 0| = |a| and |graphPoint 0 b| = |b|.
1. Bounds for v. B_r(0) is convex, v is differentiable on it (it is C^1, and 1 != 0), and |fderivWithin v B_r(0) x| <= eps there. By the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderivWithin_le, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/MeanValue.lean:484), |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2| for x1, x2 in B_r(0). Since v(0) = 0, |v x| <= eps |x|.
If x is in B°_r(0), then B_r(0) is a neighbourhood of x (closedBall_mem_nhds_of_mem). So v is C^1 at x, fderiv v x = fderivWithin v B_r(0) x (fderivWithin_of_mem_nhds), and |fderiv v x| <= eps.
2. Linear part. Define continuous linear maps A h := pi(q(graphPoint h 0)) from R^n to R^n and V h := sigma(q(graphPoint h 0)) from R^n to R^l.
By step 0, |A h|^2 + |V h|^2 = |q(graphPoint h 0)|^2 = |h|^2. By the tilt hypothesis, |V h| = infDist(q(graphPoint h 0), T0) <= vartheta |h|.
Since 0 <= vartheta <= 1, (1 - vartheta)^2 <= 1 - vartheta^2. Hence |A h|^2 >= (1 - vartheta^2)|h|^2 >= (1 - vartheta)^2 |h|^2, i.e. |A h| >= (1 - vartheta)|h| >= (11/12)|h|.
So A is injective, and in finite dimension (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo) it is a linear isomorphism of R^n with |A^{-1} k| <= (12/11)|k| for all k.
3. The chart. Put Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)), Phi(x) := pi(Psi(x)) and g(x) := pi(q(graphPoint 0 (v x))). By step 0, Phi(x) = c + A x + g(x).
For x1, x2 in B_r(0), g(x1) - g(x2) = pi(q(graphPoint 0 (v x1 - v x2))), so |g(x1) - g(x2)| <= |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2|. Also g(0) = 0.
Therefore |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2)| <= eps |x1 - x2| on B_r(0), and Phi(0) = c.
4. Injectivity estimate. For x1, x2 in B_r(0): |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2)| >= |A(x1 - x2)| - |g(x1) - g(x2)| >= (1 - vartheta - eps)|x1 - x2| >= (7/8)|x1 - x2|, because vartheta + eps <= 1/12 + 1/24 = 1/8.
5. Solving Phi(x) = w. Claim: each w in B_{r/2}(c) equals Phi(x) for some x in B_{3r/5}(0).
Let K := B_{3r/5}(0). It is contained in B_r(0) and is complete. Let F_w(x) := A^{-1}(w - c - g(x)).
For x in K: |F_w(x)| <= (12/11)(|w - c| + |g(x)|) <= (12/11)(r/2 + eps * 3r/5) <= (12/11)(r/2 + r/40) = 63r/110 < 3r/5. So F_w maps K into K.
Also |F_w(x1) - F_w(x2)| = |A^{-1}(g(x2) - g(x1))| <= (12/11) eps |x1 - x2| <= (1/22)|x1 - x2|, so F_w is a contraction of K.
By the Banach fixed point theorem F_w has a fixed point x in K. F_w(x) = x means A x = w - c - g(x), i.e. Phi(x) = w.
[Lean: ContractingWith is not imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission. The in-scope lemma ApproximatesLinearOn.surjOn_closedBall_of_nonlinearRightInverse (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/ApproximatesLinearOn.lean:143) packages exactly this argument. By step 3, Phi is ApproximatesLinearOn A on B_r(0) with constant eps. Use the nonlinear right inverse A^{-1} with nnnorm 12/11 (step 2), centre 0 and radius 3r/5. The lemma gives Phi(B_{3r/5}(0)) ⊇ B_{(11/12 - eps) 3r/5}(Phi(0)), which contains B_{r/2}(c) because Phi(0) = c and (11/12 - 1/24)(3r/5) = 21r/40 >= r/2.]
For each w in B_{r/2}(c) choose such a point x(w) in B_{3r/5}(0) with Phi(x(w)) = w. For other w set x(w) := 0.
6. Definition of f, and (b). Put f(w) := sigma(Psi(x(w))). For w in B_{r/2}(c), pi(Psi(x(w))) = Phi(x(w)) = w, so by step 0, y + q(graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))) = Psi(x(w)) = q0(graphPoint w (f w)).
Also x(w) lies in B_{3r/5}(0), which is inside B_r(0). Moreover |v x(w)| <= eps |x(w)| <= (1/24)(3r/5) = r/40, and by (ii) |graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))|^2 = |x(w)|^2 + |v x(w)|^2 <= (3r/5)^2 + (r/40)^2 < r^2. So |graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))| <= r, which is (b) with x := x(w).
7. Proof of (c). Let x be in B_r(0), w in B_{r/2}(c) and b in R^l with Psi(x) = q0(graphPoint w b). Applying pi and sigma (step 0) gives Phi(x) = w and sigma(Psi(x)) = b.
Also Phi(x(w)) = w with x(w) in B_r(0). Step 4 gives (7/8)|x - x(w)| <= |Phi(x) - Phi(x(w))| = 0, so x = x(w) and b = sigma(Psi(x(w))) = f(w).
8. Derivatives of the chart. By step 0, Psi(x) = y + q(E^{-1}(x, v x)). v is C^1 on the open ball B°_r(0) (restriction of the hypothesis), so Psi and Phi = pi ∘ Psi are C^1 on B°_r(0). Hence x -> fderiv Psi x and x -> fderiv Phi x are continuous on B°_r(0) (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
At x0 in B°_r(0), put Dv := fderiv v x0; then |Dv| <= eps by step 1. The chain rule (HasFDerivAt.prodMk, composition with continuous linear maps) gives DPsi(x0) h = q(graphPoint h (Dv h)) and DPhi(x0) = pi ∘ DPsi(x0).
Thus DPhi(x0) h = A h + pi(q(graphPoint 0 (Dv h))), so |DPhi(x0) h| >= (1 - vartheta)|h| - eps|h| >= (7/8)|h|. Hence DPhi(x0) is an injective endomorphism of R^n, i.e. a continuous linear equivalence L_{x0}, with |L_{x0}^{-1} k| <= (8/7)|k|.
Also sigma(DPsi(x0) h) = V h + sigma(q(graphPoint 0 (Dv h))), so |sigma(DPsi(x0) h)| <= vartheta |h| + eps |h| <= |h|/8.
9. x(.) is Lipschitz. For w1, w2 in B_{r/2}(c), step 4 and Phi(x(wi)) = wi give (7/8)|x(w1) - x(w2)| <= |w1 - w2|. So x(.) is (8/7)-Lipschitz, hence continuous, on B_{r/2}(c), with values in B_{3r/5}(0), which is inside B°_r(0).
10. Derivative of f and the slope bound. Fix w in B°_{r/2}(c) and put x0 := x(w). Three facts hold:
- x(.) is continuous at w (step 9);
- Phi has derivative L_{x0} at x(w) (step 8);
- Phi(x(w')) = w' for all w' in the neighbourhood B°_{r/2}(c) of w.
By the local-left-inverse rule (HasFDerivAt.of_local_left_inverse, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/OfCompLeft.lean:165), x(.) has derivative L_{x0}^{-1} at w.
By the chain rule, f = sigma ∘ Psi ∘ x(.) has derivative f'(w) := sigma ∘ DPsi(x(w)) ∘ DPhi(x(w))^{-1} at w. By step 8, |f'(w) k| <= (1/8)|DPhi(x(w))^{-1} k| <= (1/8)(8/7)|k| = |k|/7. So |fderiv f w| = |f'(w)| <= 1/7 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).
11. f is C^1 on B°_{r/2}(c). The map w -> f'(w) = sigma ∘ fderiv Psi (x(w)) ∘ (fderiv Phi (x(w)))^{-1} is continuous at each w in B°_{r/2}(c), because:
- x(.) is continuous with values in B°_r(0) (step 9);
- fderiv Psi and fderiv Phi are continuous there (step 8);
- inversion is continuous at invertible elements of the complete normed ring of endomorphisms of R^n (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Units.lean:183, with Ring.inverse(DPhi(x(w))) = L_{x(w)}^{-1}); alternatively, |P^{-1} - Q^{-1}| = |P^{-1}(Q - P)Q^{-1}| <= (8/7)^2 |P - Q| for P, Q of the form DPhi(x(.));
- a composition of continuous linear maps depends continuously on its factors.
f has derivative f'(w') at every point w' of the open set B°_{r/2}(c). Since f' is continuous at every point of B°_{r/2}(c), it is continuous on B°_{r/2}(c), which is a neighbourhood of w. So f is C^1 at w (contDiffAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt with n = 0, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:1018, together with contDiffAt_zero, Defs.lean:1129, which asks for continuity of f' on a neighbourhood of w, not just at w). Hence f is C^1 on B°_{r/2}(c), and with step 10 this is (a).
Implementation remark: the child is a single theorem with no new imports, options or helper declarations. ContractingWith and ContDiffAt.to_localInverse are not in scope; the lemmas cited above are. A direct Lean rendering of steps 0-11 compiles in a scratch copy of the pinned project under the default heartbeat limit, using between 100000 and 150000 heartbeats. The condition is that every scalar inequality is closed by linarith with explicit product hints, never by nlinarith. Typical hints are mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right applied to vartheta <= 1/12 or eps <= 1/24 and a norm, mul_nonneg (0 <= 1/8 - vartheta - eps) (norm_nonneg _), and mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (0 <= vartheta) (0 <= 1 - vartheta)) (sq_nonneg |h|) in step 2. Squared bounds use pow_le_pow_left₀, pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ and pow_left_inj₀. An otherwise identical rendering with about 15 nlinarith calls needs between 200000 and 250000 heartbeats and fails the default limit.
proof_key_steps: Coordinates pi, sigma adapted to T0: z = q0(graphPoint (pi z) (sigma z)), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z|
Mean value inequality: v is eps-Lipschitz on B_r(0), |fderiv v| <= eps inside
Tilt plus Pythagoras: A h = pi(q(graphPoint h 0)) satisfies |A h| >= (11/12)|h|, so A is invertible with |A^{-1}| <= 12/11
Phi = c + A + g with g eps-Lipschitz; injectivity |Phi x1 - Phi x2| >= (7/8)|x1 - x2| on B_r(0)
Contraction (ApproximatesLinearOn surjectivity) solves Phi(x) = w for w in B_{r/2}(c) with x in B_{3r/5}(0); define f(w) = sigma(Psi(x(w))); (b) and (c) follow
DPhi bounded below by 7/8 and |sigma ∘ DPsi| <= 1/8 on the open ball
x(.) is 8/7-Lipschitz; local-left-inverse rule gives Dx = DPhi^{-1}; |Df| <= (1/8)(8/7) = 1/7
Continuity of w -> sigma ∘ DPsi(x(w)) ∘ DPhi(x(w))^{-1} gives C^1 on the open ball

The proof constructs the inverse inside B_{3r/5}, establishes injectivity, verifies the local inverse derivative hypotheses, and obtains slope (1/8)(8/7)=1/7. Continuity of the derivative on a neighbourhood establishes C¹. All hypotheses are used correctly; only rotated_coords is required.
